Getting Started with gstIndia

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

gstIndia v2.0.0 provides nine tidy data.table datasets covering India’s GST ecosystem from July 2017 through early 2026, along with a complete suite of analysis functions. All monetary values are in Rs. Crore.

library(gstIndia)
library(data.table)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'data.table'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     %notin%

What’s in the package? 

gst_catalogue()
#>                 dataset rows              coverage
#> 1:        gst_statewise 4306 FY 2017-18 to 2025-26
#> 2:          gst_refunds 2911 FY 2020-21 to 2025-26
#> 3:         gstr1_filing 3876 FY 2017-18 to 2025-26
#> 4:        gstr3b_filing 3914 FY 2017-18 to 2025-26
#> 5:             ewb_data 3474 FY 2018-19 to 2025-26
#> 6:      igst_settlement 3914 FY 2017-18 to 2025-26
#> 7: gross_net_collection   23  Apr 2024 to Feb 2026
#> 8:     gst_registration   39     Snapshot Mar 2025
#> 9: gst_taxpayer_profile   16     Snapshot Mar 2025
#>                                                 description
#> 1:        State-wise monthly CGST/SGST/IGST/CESS collection
#> 2:              State-wise monthly GST refund disbursements
#> 3:              GSTR-1 filing compliance by state and month
#> 4:             GSTR-3B filing compliance by state and month
#> 5:          E-Way Bill statistics (intrastate & interstate)
#> 6:     Monthly IGST settlement to states (regular + ad-hoc)
#> 7: Gross vs net national GST collection with YoY comparison
#> 8:                  Taxpayer registration by state and type
#> 9:          Taxpayer constitution and female representation

Quick reference 

gst_years()      # available financial years
#> [1] "2017-18" "2018-19" "2019-20" "2020-21" "2021-22" "2022-23" "2023-24"
#> [8] "2024-25" "2025-26"
gst_states()     # 36+ states with codes and regions

1. State-wise Collection

Example: ggplot2 Trend Chart 

library(ggplot2)

top5 <- gst_top_states(n = 5, financial_year = "2023-24")$state
dt   <- gst_filter(state = top5,
                   financial_year = c("2022-23","2023-24","2024-25"),
                   component = "total")

ggplot(dt, aes(month_date, total / 1e3, colour = state)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma_format(suffix = "K Cr")) +
  labs(title    = "Monthly GST Collection — Top 5 States",
       subtitle = "FY 2022-23 to 2024-25  |  Rs. '000 Crore",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       caption  = "Source: Ministry of Finance, GoI") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Data Source

All data sourced from the Ministry of Finance, Government of India and the GST Council. Data covers July 2017 (GST rollout) through February 2026. FY 2025-26 figures are provisional.
